newsitem.title: FRANCE: France gives details of Telecom sale.
newsitem.headline: France gives details of Telecom sale.

text.p: France will sell about 20 percent of state-owned telecommunications giant France Telecom next April, Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon said in an interview published on Tuesday.
The sale, in the second half of April 1997, will be aimed mainly at private individuals, he said in the interview with financial daily La Tribune Desfosses.

He also said wanted to see a third competitor in the French telecomunications sector, alongside France Telecom and the recently formed Cegetel, a grouping of Generale des Eaux, British Telecom Plc, SBC Communications Inc and Mannesmann AG.
Analysts estimate the sale would raise between 20 billion and 40 billion francs ($7.76 billion), with the money likely to be used to fund capital injections to other state-owned companies.

Under the Maastricht treaty on monetary union, privatisation revenues cannot be used to reduce budget deficits, although France will use a special transfer from France Telecom to cover future pension liabilities to cut its deficit next year.

Among various companies requiring capital injections is state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais, whose chairman last week suggested it would need some eight to nine billion francs in recapitalisation if it were to be privatised quickly.
This would be on top of several billion francs expected to be required to fund a new rescue plan for the bank.
Fillon's comments on the partial sale of France Telecom confirm suggestions by chairman Michel Bon who has said he expected a first share sale in April.

A spokeswoman at Fillon's ministry was unavailable for comment on the timing of the sale of a second tranche, which analysts have said is unlikely before liberalisation of the European telecommunications sector in 1998.
The French government has said it will sell a total of 49 percent of France Telecom, with 10 percent earmarked for France Telecom staff.
"The first tranche due in the second half of April (1997), should cover about 20 percent of the capital," Fillon said in the interview.
"The general idea is to carry out the largest public offering ever in France. France Telecom has 32 million customers, that's a fantastic starting point."
"Our target is to be at least as ambitious as Deutsche Telekom, which is aiming for two million individual shareholders," Fillon said.
Asked about speculation that 20 percent of France Telecom's capital would be reserved for a cross-shareholding with Deutsche Telekom, he said this may be too high.

"Before deciding on the cross-shareholding with Deutsche Telekom, we must know the value of the German and French operators. Taking into account the foreseeable value of the companies, 20 percent seems to me financially high," he said.
Fillon said he was pleased at General des Eaux's creation of the Cegetel telecoms grouping but said a third big company was desirable to ensure competition played its part in the market.

"We had the example of mobile telephones, a sector where it took a third competitor for competition to play its full role and for the market to develop," he said. "I would like therefore to see a third operator created."
